name: Structured-Tree Arterial Outflow Boundary Condition
summary: Use recursively scaled distal vascular trees to derive terminal pressure-flow impedance for proximal vessel models.
core_idea: Represent unresolved distal arteries as a structured network and compute an effective dynamic impedance boundary.
innovation: Preserves frequency-dependent wave reflections beyond a pure resistance or simple lumped terminal.
limitations: Depends on distal tree geometry and constitutive assumptions.
Additional frequency-domain calculations may complicate coupling.

start_here.why: Influential physiological outflow formulation for truncated arterial networks.
start_here.focus: Structured distal tree assumptions and terminal impedance construction.

curation_note: Core method concept and checked source(s) recorded; suggested readings remain advisory and may be revised.
